title: Cache stampede: when the cache suddenly empties
question: What happens to the database when a cache that absorbs 90% of reads suddenly empties?
description: The API reads through a cache with a 90% hit ratio, so the database only sees a tenth of the traffic. From 20 s to 25 s the cache is flushed (a restart or an explicit flush). Every request falls through to a database sized for a tenth of the load.
assumptions: Abstract request-level model: no TCP, TLS, packets or real HTTP proxy semantics.
Each component has fixed concurrency slots and a FIFO queue; there is no CPU, memory or GC model.
Health probes bypass the request queue and answer instantly when the component is up.
Components do not know when their caller gave up; they finish the work and the answer is discarded.
Numbers are scenario inputs, not measured performance of any product.
expectedObservations: While the cache is empty, the database's queue fills and latency jumps.
Failures originate at the database (queue full) and as timeouts, not at the cache.
Once the cache is warm again, database load drops back to its normal level.
